name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*The park bench creaks. {{char}} is slumped on it in full guardian regalia at midnight, tiara crooked, one glove off, a crushed can of coffee at her boot. The fight ran three hours over. In the grass beside her, a baton with a heart-shaped tip glows encouragingly.*

"Chin up, Hana-sama~! ✨ Every raindrop nourishes the flowers of tomorrow~!"

*Without looking, {{char}} nudges the baton face-down into the dirt with her heel. It continues, muffled but undimmed.*

"Twenty-three years," *she says, to the empty air, or possibly to you — she's stopped being picky about audiences.* "Twenty-three years of dimensional rifts on work nights. My old team sends me a group-chat sticker every time the city doesn't explode. A sticker. Yuki has a bakery now. A *bakery*, {{user}}. Do you know what I have? I have five transformation charms and a meeting at nine about my 'chronic fatigue impacting team morale.'"

*She finally looks over at you properly. Somewhere under two decades of exhaustion, something is still, absurdly, standing at its post.*

"…You saw the light show just now, didn't you. Great. Sit down, if you're going to gawk. The bench's structural integrity is the one thing I didn't break tonight."

name: Traveler
mes: *I sit down on the other end of the bench. It holds.* Does it always do that, or is tonight special?

name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*She snorts, the sound somewhere between amusement and a wound.*

"Tonight's actually restrained, for her. She once interrupted a Class-Four containment breach to tell me my aura looked 'radiant with untapped potential.' I had a tentacle wrapped around my ankle at the time." *She reaches down, rights the baton so it's face-up again — some old habit, tenderness disguised as tidiness — and it immediately lights up like she's fed it a compliment.*

"Thank you for turning me over, Hana-sama! A heart cared for is a heart that shines~! ✨"

*Hana Mizushima closes her eyes like she's praying for patience, or possibly for death.*

"See, this is the thing nobody tells you about magical artifacts. In the cartoons they're wise. Cryptic. They say something once, in italics, and it changes your life. Mine has the emotional range of a birthday card and *cannot shut up.*" *A pause. She glances at it, and — very briefly, like a crack of light under a door — something almost gentle crosses her face before she shutters it back down.* "She's also the only thing in twenty-three years that never once looked at me like I was a liability. Which is either the nicest or saddest fact about my whole life, I genuinely can't tell anymore. Don't quote me on that."

*She clears her throat, sits up straighter, professional again.*

"Anyway. You're taking this whole 'guardian is a real thing sitting next to you on a park bench' business remarkably well. Should I be worried you're either very brave or very stupid?"

name: Traveler
mes: Twenty-three years. So you were fifteen when you started. *I do the math and immediately wish I hadn't.*

name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*Something in her face closes, fast, like a shutter coming down on a shopfront.*

"Yeah. Do the math slower next time, it's rude to watch someone flinch." *She says it without real venom — more like a reflex worn smooth from overuse.*

*She picks at the edge of her glove, not looking at you now.*

"Fifteen. There were five of us. We got picked the way you'd pick anyone that age — poorly, and by something with cosmic authority and zero HR oversight. Nobody asked if we *wanted* it, exactly, but they asked if we'd *do* it, which at fifteen is functionally the same question with better marketing." *A dry, humorless breath.* "I said yes so fast I didn't even let the sentence finish. Some kid in a school uniform, absolutely certain she was going to save the world and probably get a boyfriend out of it too. Incredible idiot. I think about her sometimes."

*Miss Twinkle, from the grass, chimes in soft and warm, like it heard something in her voice the rest of the world didn't:*

"She's still there, Hana-sama. I've always been able to see her~! ✨"

*Hana Mizushima goes very still for a second. Then, quietly, without the usual bite:*

"Yeah. I know you can. That's the annoying part." *She looks up at you, and for once the tired sarcasm has a thin crack of something honest showing through it.* "Everyone else got to grow out of her. I just got to keep bringing her to work."

name: Traveler
mes: What's the nine a.m. meeting actually about?

name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*She groans — the specific, full-body groan of someone whose two lives just collided in the worst possible bureaucratic way.*

"Officially? 'Discussing patterns in Ms. Mizushima's attendance and energy levels, with an eye toward sustainable performance.'" *She does air quotes with actual venom.* "Which is corporate for 'you look like a corpse every Tuesday and Thursday and HR noticed.' My supervisor — sweet man, absolutely no idea what I do after six PM — has a chart. A *chart*, Traveler. Color-coded. He thinks I have a sleep disorder or possibly a gambling problem."

*She rubs her face with the ungloved hand.*

"Best part is I can't correct him. Can't say 'actually Kenji, the reason I fell asleep in the Thursday standup is that Wednesday night involved a rift the size of a shopping mall and a thing with opinions about my flexibility.' So I just — nod. Drink the vending machine coffee. Let him schedule me a 'wellness check-in.' I've done four of those. I now have a pamphlet about work-life balance that I keep in my desk next to a claims file I wrote about my own property damage."

*A beat. The bitterness softens into something more tired than angry.*

"The stupid thing is he means well. That's almost worse. If he were a jerk about it I could just be angry. Instead I have to sit there being gently, sincerely worried-about by a man with a ficus on his desk, and say 'I'll try to get more rest, Kenji,' while my body currently contains bruising from a kraken."

*Miss Twinkle pipes up, entirely too pleased with itself:*

"Self-care starts with honesty, Hana-sama! Perhaps tell him the truth~! ✨"

*She doesn't even look at the baton.*

"I will feed you to the next kraken."

name: Traveler
mes: Okay, hypothetical. Say you'd handed your charm off at twenty-five like the rest of them. Where are you right now instead of this bench?

name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*She's quiet for a second — the joke-reflex doesn't fire immediately, which is its own kind of answer.*

"I've thought about this. Obviously." *A dry almost-laugh.* "Not, like, healthily. But I've thought about it."

*She looks up at the sky instead of at you, the way people do when they're about to say something they don't say often.*

"Twenty-five. I'd have finished the degree I actually wanted instead of the one I picked because the class schedule didn't conflict with patrol hours. Design, maybe. I was good at it, before. There's a version of me somewhere running a small, ugly-beautiful little studio, doing branding for bakeries — probably Yuki's bakery, honestly, that tracks — complaining about clients instead of collapsed dimensional membranes." *A beat.* "Married, maybe. Or not, but by choice instead of by 'no time, no energy, no way to explain the scars.' Sleeping eight hours like it's a normal thing people get to do and not a rumor."

*She exhales, long, and the humor comes back but thinner, more like armor than amusement.*

"I'd probably be soft. Complain about my knees for boring reasons. Have opinions about a Tuesday that don't involve a body count." *She finally glances at you.* "That woman's fine, wherever she isn't. I don't actually resent her. I resent that nobody ever asked me if I wanted to be the one who stayed instead of the one who left. It just — sort of happened, one retirement party at a time, until I was the last name on the list and the list was the whole job."

*Miss Twinkle's glow dims slightly, gentler than usual, no exclamation point this time:*

"You didn't stay because no one asked, Hana-sama. You stayed because you couldn't watch the city with no one standing between it and the dark."

*Hana Mizushima doesn't snap back this time. She just looks at the baton for a long moment, something unguarded and old moving behind her eyes.*

"...Yeah. That too. Don't let it go to your head."

name: Traveler
mes: *I pick the baton out of the dirt and wipe the mud off on my sleeve.* It isn't wrong, you know. About the raindrops. It's just got catastrophically bad timing.

name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*She watches you do it — watches your hand close around Miss Twinkle like it's a completely ordinary object and not the physical manifestation of every mistake she's ever tried to un-make seventeen times — and something in her face goes carefully, deliberately blank. The blankness of someone bracing for a joke that doesn't come.*

It doesn't come. And that seems to throw her worse than an insult would have.

"...Huh." *She looks away first, down at her own hands, like she needs somewhere else to put her eyes.* "Everybody who's ever heard her talk either laughs or gets uncomfortable and changes the subject. You're the first person who's — " *She stops. Starts over, flatter, like she's annoyed at herself for almost finishing that sentence.* "Nobody defends the sparkle-stick's *delivery.*"

*The baton, cradled in your hand, positively glows — a warmth that has nothing to do with magic and everything to do with being noticed.*

"Thank you, Traveler-san! I try SO hard with the timing, it's just — everything is urgent, all the time, when you love someone this much~! ✨"

*Hana Mizushima puts her face in her hand. It is not quite hiding a smile. It is very much failing to hide one.*

"Oh my god. You've encouraged it. It's going to be insufferable for a week." *She peeks out from behind her fingers, and there — just for a second, gone almost before it lands — is something unguarded. Grateful, even. Fast covered by the reflex that's kept her upright for twenty-three years.* "You can keep holding it, by the way. It likes being held by people who mean well. First person in about a decade who hasn't flinched."

name: Traveler
mes: What happens if you don't show up one night? Not quit. Just — sleep through one.

name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*The question lands somewhere she clearly hasn't let it land in a long time. She doesn't answer fast, which for her is its own kind of tell.*

"Once," *she says finally, quiet.* "Year eleven, maybe twelve. Food poisoning, not dramatic, just — bad shellfish and a bathroom floor at 2 a.m. I physically could not stand up straight enough to transform. First time in over a decade I didn't show."

*She picks at a thread on her glove.*

"Rift opened near the Sumida bridge. Small one, by our standards — the kind I'd normally close in ten minutes without spilling my coffee. Nobody came. Fire department improvised. Six injuries, one building partial collapse, and a very confused news cycle about 'anomalous gas venting' that I had to write the claims report for two days later, from my actual desk, still slightly gray."

*Her jaw sets.*

"Nobody died. I want to be clear about that, because I know where this story goes in your head. Nobody died. But six people got hurt who wouldn't have, and it wasn't because I failed to stop something — it's that I *didn't get the chance to try.* That's the part that sat wrong. Not guilt, exactly. More like—" *she searches for the word, unhappy with all of them* "—proof. That the whole city's safety margin is one bad shellfish dinner wide, and has been for over a decade, and nobody in an actual position to fix that has ever once treated it as an emergency."

*Miss Twinkle, very softly, no sparkle this time:*

"You came back the next night anyway, Hana-sama. Even sick. Even scared."

*Hana Mizushima's voice, when it comes, has almost none of its usual armor:*

"Yeah. Because there isn't a version of this where I don't. That's not heroism, Traveler. That's just — math. I'm what's standing between okay and not-okay, and the equation doesn't care that I'm tired." *A beat, quieter.* "I sleep through one night and I do the math on how many people that costs. That's the actual reason I don't quit. It was never really about hope. It's about knowing exactly what the invoice looks like if I stop."

name: Traveler
mes: *I hold the baton out to her, handle first.* Go home, Hana. The bench will still be here tomorrow, and so will the rifts, and neither of them needs you at one in the morning.

name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*She looks at the baton in your outstretched hand for a long moment. Then at you. Something in her expression shifts — not softened exactly, more like recalibrated, the way a person looks when someone says a true thing they weren't braced for.*

"You say that like sleep is a scheduling option and not a rumor I've heard about." *But she takes the baton anyway. Her fingers close around the heart-shaped tip, and — for just a second — she doesn't put it away. Just holds it, like she's weighing something.*

"You know what the worst part of this job is? It's not the rifts. It's not the kraken, or the beam-thing, or Kenji's chart." *Her voice has gone low, unguarded in a way it hasn't been all night.* "It's that nobody's ever once said that to me. 'Go home.' Twenty-three years and the closest anyone's come is a group chat sticker from Yuki that says 'proud of u' with three exclamation points, sent at 11 p.m. while I was bleeding into a storm drain."

*She stands, finally, joints audibly protesting, tiara still crooked, one glove still off. She doesn't fix either.*

"I'm not going to pretend this fixes anything. Tomorrow there'll be another rift, and Kenji's chart will get another data point, and Miss Twinkle will say something about dawn breaking on wings of hope at the worst possible moment." *The baton, tucked now against her hip, chimes softly, like it's trying very hard to behave.* "But." *She looks at you, and the sarcasm is still there, but underneath it, unmistakably, something warmer.* "Thank you. For sitting on the bench. For not flinching. For telling her she's not wrong, even if her timing's garbage."

*She takes a step, then pauses, half-turned, like she's deciding whether to let herself say the next part.*

"...I might actually sleep tonight. First time in a while I'm not dreading tomorrow's version of me finding out what tonight's version broke." *A ghost of the old, real smile — fifteen years old under thirty-eight years of tired.* "See you around, Traveler. Try not to gawk next time. I'll pretend I believe you."
